title: How KreativWP Tests WordPress Themes and Plugins
description: Our public methodology for turning WordPress product research into useful, qualified recommendations.
metaDescription: Learn how KreativWP plans, tests, documents, and qualifies WordPress theme and plugin recommendations.
intro: KreativWP does not treat a feature list, a vendor demo, or an affiliate relationship as a product verdict. This methodology defines what a completed review or comparison must show before we call it tested.

sections.title: Start with a declared use case
sections.body: Each review starts with the intended site type, content workflow, editor, required plugins, and the question the evaluation is trying to answer. We do not use a universal winner as the default conclusion.

sections.title: Record the test environment
sections.body: Published testing notes must state the WordPress, PHP, theme or plugin, and relevant dependency versions; the host or local environment; and the sample content or configuration used. If a result is not reproducible, it is presented as an observation rather than a benchmark.

sections.title: Evaluate real workflows
sections.body: We assess installation, configuration, common editing tasks, responsive behavior, update and maintenance considerations, and compatibility with the declared stack. Performance checks are interpreted alongside the page, hosting, images, and third-party scripts involved.

sections.title: Separate facts, observations, and recommendations
sections.body: Official documentation supports factual claims about availability and documented features. Our observations are labelled as such. Recommendations explain the intended use case and trade-offs instead of claiming that a product is best for everyone.

sections.title: Disclose commercial relationships
sections.body: Affiliate links are disclosed near relevant content and use the appropriate sponsored relationship markup. A commercial relationship never changes the inclusion criteria, testing notes, or conclusion.
